style.vernacular: Mixed city: Ottoman-era mosques with stone domes and slim minarets and a few old stone-and-timber houses; Yugoslav-era concrete blocks and brutalist/modernist public buildings (Rilindja tower, National Library with its 99 domes under a metal mesh); post-1999 reinforced-concrete houses and apartment blocks with infill brick, often left unrendered or painted in pale pastels, with red or grey tile and metal roofs; newer glass-and-render offices, malls and university buildings.
style.ornament: Ottoman-derived domes and pencil minarets on mosques; Yugoslav modernist concrete grids and brutalist massing; metal-mesh clad domes of the National Library; rough unrendered brick infill on concrete frames; marble paving on central squares.

sources.what: Ottoman mosques with prayer hall, porch, minaret and cupola; Yugoslav-era modernism and brutalism; National Library with domes; kulla stone towers
99 domes of various sizes, exterior covered in metal mesh, about 16,500 m2, inaugurated 1982 (Mutnjakovic)
